subject.title: Provider key pools + bucket-aware cooldown/backoff on 429 (Gemini projects) to prevent retry storms

question: Should Gemini/API-key bucket-aware cooldown be folded into the broader provider-profile pool-routing contract, implemented as a narrower key-bucket cooldown feature, or left to external sidecar/plugin experimentation until a core API is chosen?
rationale: The missing behavior is real, but it defines new public routing/config and persisted quota-state semantics that automation should not invent without maintainer direction.

options.title: Fold Into Provider-Pool Routing
options.body: Use the open provider-profile routing design to cover API keys, OAuth profiles, quota buckets, status visibility, and strategy defaults in one upgrade-safe contract.

options.title: Ship A Narrow Key-Bucket Feature
options.body: Add only key bucket metadata and cooldown rotation for direct API-key providers while deferring broader pool scheduling and concurrency semantics.

options.title: Defer To External Prototype
options.body: Keep current core behavior and let the sidecar/plugin pattern prove the needed API seam before adding core configuration.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Provider-Pool Routing
recommendation.body: Use the open provider-profile routing design to cover API keys, OAuth profiles, quota buckets, status visibility, and strategy defaults in one upgrade-safe contract.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest available owner signal for the current rate-limit rotation cap, maintainer follow-up, and merge decision around adjacent provider fallback semantics.
